title: Requires Subscription
text: Unreasonable pricing options.

title: Requires Subscription
text: This app only allows you to list a total of #10 items on/in your inventory for free.  Anything more than #10 items requires a subscription.  They do allow you to have a ten day free trial, but that’s it.  An app with such a simplistic use should be free to use because this is nothing that you can’t do on your cell phone for free in the ‘Notes’ section, etc.

title: Definitely not a free app. Free for 10 items is a joke
text: If your app is paid, list it as paid. The subscription service for apps like this which should be a one time purchases is garbage. Do not support this garbage business model.

title: Useful, but subscription based.
text: I like this app, I really do.   I’ve paid the subscription for about 3 or 4 years, but I’m stopping now.    I think subscription software is ridiculous.   If you were a newspaper, with reporters going out everyday to gather the news, I might consider it, but you’re a piece of software, and bug fixes and small incremental upgrades just aren’t worth it.  It should just be a one time charge of some sort, I’m perfectly willing to pay for software, but not indefinitely..

title: Say “No” to Subscriptions
text: I honestly cannot fathom why this requires a subscription instead of a one-time purchase. This is not normal. I don’t want to wonder why I’m getting charged a year or two from now for something I haven’t used very much. That’s essentially what apps that require subscriptions are counting on.

title: Great Concept, but…
text: There is absolutely no reason this needs to be a subscription service. I would pay $5-$10 for this app as a one-time purchase, but a recurring payment indefinitely is absurd.

title: Import issue
text: The ability to import from a CSV file seems corrupted, with the option sometimes being there and sometimes not. AI says this is a known issue and offered several reasonable solutions, but none of them worked. I'm not going to subscribe to an app that is glitchy right out the gate.

title: Needs Additional Refinement
text: I am a new user of this software, and I understood from its user manual that my data would be synced and backed-up in iCould, which is what the developer recommends. I learned the hard way that “syncing” and “back-up” are not the same thing even though the terms are used interchangeably. I accidentally melted some data and when I tried to recover a back-up from iCloud, I discovered the data was also deleted from the iCloud ‘back-up.” Under My Roof should be REALLY clear that a user must manually save a back-up to the user’s desktop hard drive or to an external hard drive. There needs to be an option in preferences giving users the ability to automatically save backups in a specific location because if the users doesn’t, there isn’t a back-up made. Apple tech support said that data from Under My Roof is not a back-up and shouldn’t be considered as one. Under My Roof only uses iCloud to sync data.

title: Ease of Use
text: I do like this app and understand it is multi faceted to its credit and it isn’t necessarily going to be easy to learn all the aspects of it right away. However, it is very difficult to follow the tutorials; given how fast the narrator speaks (fair to say this isn’t the only app that is like this). Also, I’ve been unable to find specific answers to basic issues i.e. sync status. It says its idle or disabled test no solution. Finally, some of us are trying to create a legacy type record and are at an age that may make it difficult to follow along with disjointed training guides. Hope my expectations are reasonable since we are paying a fee.

title: Needs lifetime purchase option
text: Please.

title: Repairs and Changes need work
text: I’ve spent a lot of time adding Repairs and Changes in the Mac app for various locations. When I look in the iOS app, they are nowhere to be found. The ones added under the Home show up, but not under Locations. All I see in the app is the Inventory list. I looked at their help documentation and videos thinking I must be looking in the wrong place, but all of that is outdated and does not represent the current UI. Another feature that would be really appreciated is the ability to move an entry after it’s been added. For example, adjust a Change to a Repair or move it to a different Location. Also, the ability to pull up all Changes across all Locations into one list. One use case I have for the app is to easily pull up adjustments to my house cost basis, but that requires me to go to each location and tally up the total by hand. Unfortunately, the app seems very Inventory focused, which is not what I care that much about.

title: Requires a subscription.
text: Wish it was a one time fee. It’s too tricky to get out of subscriptions these days so I avoid them like a plague!    I’ll just buy a paper ledger .  $20 for 10 years vs $300 for 10 years.   Sometimes you just can’t beat the good old days ;-).

title: Great Product… Will be a Lifetime user
text: Great Product, developer always adds positive enhancements that make this an excellent app for both desktop and iOS. Keep up the great work!

title: Some new features are nice, but data input steps backward
text:
I upgraded from Home Inventory in spite of the subscription modelbecuase I wanted the cloud based features. Unfortunately data entry has become much more tedious, requiring switching from keyboard to mouse too often and requiring extra mouse clicks to do the same things I could do easier with Home Inventory. If there is a drop-down category like Category, I can no longer tab to the field and either type in a couple of letters or use the down arrow key to select the category, I have to leave the keyboard and use the mouse to select the field (tabbing just skips over it), and then select from the drop-down list, which can be quite lengthy.  Also cannot tab to the Tags abd start typing, but have to move to the mouse to even select the field and then find the right tab in the (graphic, not list format) display and click on it. Data entry is taking at least 25% longer per item.

One thing I would like to see is two buttons instead of the single   icon to add a new item. One button for a new blank recors (same as the   icon) and another button for copy the last selected item into a new record, so that only a few fields need to be updated in the new record.

title: Bummer!
text: So I would have to say that this would be a great app except it requires you to pay for it with an sub.

title: Yet another subscription, not a purchase
text:
I'm tired of subscription based products.  As an inventory program goes, this one is not bad.  However, paying a monthly subscription for a tool like this just doesn't make sense.  The vendor, unfortunately, makes you waste your time by not telling you it is a subscription.  It just states, "in-app purchase".  OK, so here is the rub.... It is limited to 10 records unless you pay $4/month forever.

My suggestion is that you find an open source product that will be around in 10 years.

title: Nice but limited
text: I like the ability to document individual items in a collection, however What I was also seeking is to print the items in some form of documentation (like a catalog).  Printing seems to be limited to only 1 item at a time.

title: Looks good, no native label generation
text:
I like the look of it and appreciate that it's multi-platform.

I wanted it to be my one-stop inventory system. It didn't quite work out that way.

I had thought its support for Barcode/QRcode meant that it had the ability to generate a sharable code-image so I could use a label printer like the B21 to put it on my boxes and other inventory items.

Unfortunately that's not something it can do, and after an informative conversation with tech support it's not something they're planning to add.

I'm giving it 3 stars because it seems nice, but having to use a different app to tell this app what an id is ... well I want to make inventory managment easy and having to use a different app to tell this app what an id is every time sounds less-easy, more like a pain. 

Maybe I'll just use the gps coordinates in my ipad's photos.

title: While it seems like a good idea, I’m not here for another subscription!
text: I deleted it within about two minutes of downloading it. Had I known it was a subscription service, I wouldn’t have downloaded it in the first place.

title: Good but expensive
text: I was hoping it would be free or at least be able to pay one time and be done with it. But no. If you want more than 10 items in your inventory you have to pay monthly or yearly.

title: Missing Key Features
text: Being able to define multiple "Homes" is a distinct advantage but the loss of reporting or to download saved documents, like receipts, is terrible.  I will continue to to use Home Inventory until these features are restored.

title: Subscription Only = No Thanks
text: Developers that think subscription model should automatically apply to them can kick rocks. There's no reason this app should cost $25-48 PER YEAR. Give an option for a one time purchase, and move on, otherwise, I (and many others) move on from you immediately. It's the difference between a 5 star and a 1 star, simple as that.

title: Free 7-day trial ...
text: If it's a free trial for 7 days, with extremely limited functionality during that trial, it's NOT a free app and should not be included when searching for actually free apps. And that's all I have to say.

text:
[EDIT based on reply from support]: Thank you for the information. I will try these out again and update my review.

title: A Database System That Can’t Edit Multiple Items?
text: Got this app after a lot of research in prep for a big move. First off: whole interface is way, way way too complicated and cross-layered. Moving Boxes, Rooms, Categories…I get that it’s meant to be versatile but right out of the box there are no real templates or intuitively designed workflows. Second: ISBN/UPC scanning and lookup NEVER works. I have scanned older paperbacks, brand new hardcovers, Blu-rays…9/10 the app returns no info, and the 1/10 it gets anything it’s totally wrong. I have no idea how in 2022 with all the barcode scanner lookup apps out there this one still doesn’t work. Third: no apparent ability to select multiple entries and then edit their notes/info as a group (think “Get Info” for multiple items in Apple Music app). You can apparently only edit a few things like tags which are meaningless to me. But when I spent two hours scanning and logging my bookshelves, only to realize I hadn’t added “Author” fields to them, I figured it would be easy to just add that field to the template, then go in and select like thirty Stephen King books and add the author name to them all simultaneously. WRONG. Which means basically this entire app is useless; if I can’t use the barcode scan then I have to manually enter in everything. And if I have to manually enter in everything then realize later I can’t easily do a mass edit, that means this thing doesn’t save me any time OR effort and actually is designed in such a way that it increases the risk of entry error. Fourth: it’s hard to find a user manual unless you basically Google and hunt for it. There should be a manual link right in the app’s help function, or at least at the dev website right up front. Instead you have to hunt through the FAQ and happen to find the Q that asks for a manual and then chase down the rabbit hole to download (in my case, only to find it couldn’t do anything I crucially needed it to). Fifth: little irritating and unnecessary problems such as adding “Author” field to the item entry template…but if I then select the category “Books” the Author field DISAPPEARS. Why?! Why should properly categorizing an item as a book cause one field to disappear and why should it be the one most SPECIFIC field relevant to BOOKS other than title? Last: all of these things combined means I think the subscription pricing model is criminal. Please don’t tell us the scripted song and dance about how charging subscription fees sustains your development and features such as “barcode scanning & lookup” when as pointed out that feature never reliably has worked for me. And not only that but literally EVERY database management system whether it’s Apple Music or Microsoft Xcel all have as one of their most BASIC ELEMENTARY functions the ability to easily select and mass edit entries. Missing that feels like the devs failed to see even the most inherent functions of database design, which considering how long they’ve had since Home Inventory (and how many months of my fees paid) is utterly inexcusable. I am extremely disappointed and would give this zero stars if I could. I will be canceling & uninstalling this app first thing in the morning, and not only urge people to find another app until this gone gets its act together, but perhaps Apple should consider delisting it from the App Store because I consider it arguably fraudulent to sell us a monthly charged app that doesn’t actually see significant development month to month, especially when it’s still missing hugely fundamental functions (imagine buying a car only to find that long the designers haven’t gotten around or even thought to work in a steering wheel—that’s what failing to allow group edits is to me).

text: Not buying an annual (or monthly!) subscription for vapor/copyware.  Nice polish but you are absolutely dreaming.  Deleted immediately.

title: bait and switch
text: I absolutely hate it when the only way you find out that to be useful you have to pay for a subscription AFTER you go through the installation and set up.

title: Maintenance triggered by Vehicle Mileage?
text: Overall good first impression of interface and ease. Would be my go to app if it had logic based on dynamic rather than predictable or "scheduled" maintenance. Triggers based on "current vehicle mileage" as an example, would make this my go to app for home/garage/workshop inventory and maintenance.

title: Why subscription?
text: Honestly this whole subscription thing for every app is getting out of control. I’d prefer to pay full price and keep the functionality I bought for the price and if in 2 years there is something new and worth to pay I’d pay to upgrade but not every year/month.

title: OK but lacking in some areas as of now
text: The app itself seems quite good, generally well featured, but it lacks some basic things such as any help files or other documentation, and there is no link within the app to the developer's support resources. This makes it quite difficult to learn about features, or lack thereof, efficiently. The app also needs additional preference settings, such as the ability to select which location view you wish to have as a default (for instance, for my use I'd prefer to be able to set it to showing all items). I'm sure the app will develop over time, but for now I'd rate it as a "good beginning".

title: Subscription disappointment
text: For an app that you will probably use a lot up front and very seldom after that, a subscription model just doesn't make sense. Charge me a one-time $20 and I'd happily pay.
